subject: RCA: inference regression impacting batch scoring - concise summary & action items
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jared Coleman <jared.coleman@finclip.com>, Rina Patel <r.patel@finclip.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brief RCA and immediate actions for yesterday's regression

Hi Jared / Rina,

Thanks again for your patience while we finished the internal analysis. Below is a concise RCA, a short timeline, and the near-term actions we've taken and committed to. I aimed to keep this focused; the attached timeline PDF has full traces and token-level metrics.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Impact window: 2028-10-30 02:10:00 UTC - 2028-10-30 03:52:00 UTC.
- Observed effects: increased per-request latency (median +2.1s), ~4.6% of FinClip batch scoring jobs returned truncated or mismatched outputs during the window.
- Root cause: a coordinated rollout of a quantized model variant (v2.1-q4) to a subset of GPU pools coincided with a change to KV-prefix cache eviction threshold. Under the workload spike the new kernel/quantization path produced unexpected token alignment in a small subset of sequences, which caused the serving runtime to retry and fall back in a way that increased tail latency and, for some long batches, produced truncated outputs.

Immediate mitigations performed (completed within 90 minutes of detection)
1) Rollback: reverted model serving traffic to v1.3 (pre-quantization) for all FinClip routes.
2) Disabled the new prefix-KV caching threshold to prevent asymmetric cache state under the observed concurrency pattern.
3) Deployed kernel scheduler patch to prevent the retry cascade in the quantized path (hotfix applied to affected pools).
4) Reprocessed affected batch jobs where feasible; see notes on verification below.

Action items and owners
- Karthik Iyer: deliver kernel scheduler fix (patch attached) and coordinate a staged re-introduction plan — ETA: 2028-11-03.
- Hannah Schmitt: update ops runbook with the cache-threshold rollback and detection heuristics — ETA: 2028-11-02.
- Marissa Cole: compensation proposal and customer-facing acceptance flow for affected billing window — ETA: 2028-11-01.
- Olga Petrov (me): convene post-incident verification call and provide final evidence pack — proposing Thu 2028-11-01 10:00 PT.

Verification we ran
- Replayed a representative sample of affected jobs against v1.3: token outputs matched expected baselines for 100% of the sample.
- End-to-end request logs for FinClip show no writes to customer-owned persistent storage that could have been corrupted.

Attachments included: clipped_rca_timeline.pdf (timeline + traces), fix-patch-1.patch (kernel scheduler), ops-runbook-update.md (draft).

Please let us know whether you want a short walk-through of the attached timeline or prefer the verification notes only. We can also start an audit run to re-score the full set of affected batches if you want us to proceed.

Apologies for the disruption. We take incidents like this very seriously and will prioritize both remediation and preventive controls.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[attachment: clipped_rca_timeline.pdf (pdf)] [attachment: fix-patch-1.patch (patch)]

From: Jared Coleman <jared.coleman@finclip.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Rina Patel <r.patel@finclip.com>, FinClip Support <support@finclip.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Oct 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brief RCA and immediate actions for yesterday's regression

Olga — thanks for the quick summary. A few clarifying items before we lock the verification: 

1) Can you quantify the total number of FinClip requests affected (absolute count) during the window and confirm whether any of those results were persisted into our downstream databases?
2) You note reprocessing of "feasible" jobs — which jobs were not reprocessed and why?
3) We will need a formal statement that our SLA credits will be applied and an outline of the compensation calculation. Marissa, please include the terms you'd propose.

Also, can you confirm that reintroducing the quantized path will have an A/B plan with throttled traffic and automated rollback triggers? Our legal/compliance team may want that in writing before we permit a re-rollout.

If it's helpful, we can take the verification call on Thu but prefer a short agenda: (1) absolute impact numbers, (2) verification evidence that no persisted corruption occurred, (3) re-rollout guardrails.

Best,
Jared
VP, ML Platforms
FinClip

Date: Thu, 01 Nov 2028 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Brief RCA and immediate actions for yesterday's regression — numbers and evidence pack

Jared / Rina,

Thanks for the quick questions. Attached is the evidence pack and a short impact table; key points below. The attached Drive link has the full set of traces and job ids for your internal audit.

Key numbers (absolute)
- Total FinClip requests in impact window: 23,814 requests.
- Requests with degraded outputs (truncated/misaligned): 1,100 requests (~4.62%).
- Persisted downstream writes observed during window: 0. No FinClip write IDs in our logs during the window indicate corrupted or partial writes.

Reprocessing status
- Reprocessed: 18,200 of the affected jobs (these were queued and re-run as part of our reprocessing campaign; results compared to baseline and validated).
- Not reprocessed: 1,100 jobs that were time-window-archived by FinClip's downstream retention (we flagged them and included full raw request/response records in the evidence pack so your team can choose a re-run or re-score).

Re-rollout plan for quantized path (v2.1-q4)
- Staged canary: 0.5% traffic for 72 hours, synthetic load injection and token-alignment checks.
- Automatic rollback triggers: >0.5% error rate in token alignment mismatch OR median latency increase >350ms over baseline for 30m.
- Manual gates: signoff required from FinClip CS or FinClip Platform before increasing beyond canary.

Attachments included in this email: clipped_rca_timeline.pdf (full traces), ops-runbook-update.md (draft with detection hooks), fix-patch-1.patch (kernel scheduler hotfix), reprocessing_manifest.csv (job ids).

Next steps we propose
1) Marissa will share a compensation proposal (billing credit) by EOD (her email below).
2) We recommend a 30-minute verification call Thursday 11/01 10:00 PT to walk the evidence pack and agree on the reprocessing approach for the 1,100 archived jobs.
3) Karthik will coordinate a dry-run of the canary with your platform team; we'll provide a detailed playbook.

If this looks right, please confirm the call time and Marissa will send an invite.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
